svg.title: SATB2-dependent gene programs in CA1 sublayer identity and inhibitory circuitry
svg.desc: Neuroday research poster. Measured RNA changes in CA1 after postnatal Satb2 deletion, gene programs, candidate intercellular signals and proposed chromatin and physiology assays.

g.text: CA1 sublayer identity and inhibitory circuitry
Mujahid Ali, Nico Wahl, Georg Dechant, Galina Apostolova
Institute for Neuroscience, Medical University of Innsbruck, Austria
When does SATB2 shape a memory circuit?
SATB2 helps active cortical neurons reorganize chromatin.
Embryonic loss strengthens PV input to superficial CA1 neurons.
We test how postnatal loss affects CA1 gene expression and circuitry.
P60 RNA · early line · 6 WT + 6 cKO

g.title: Hippocampal nuclei, CA1 layer programs and inhibitory clusters
g.desc: Seurat classification across wild-type and Satb2 conditional knockout mice. A common stem branches into five major cell types. The excitatory branch expands into CA1 and prosubiculum cluster markers and their layer assignments. The inhibitory branch shows all original clusters with C6 divided into three SST subclusters. Each terminal cluster has its own color. Superficial and deep layer markers are ranked by paired wild-type expression. Branch widths are schematic. Hover over a marker or ribbon to read the original cluster identifier.

text.tspan: RNA fell 52% in superficial and 36% in deep CA1.

g.title: CA1 sampling branches into nuclear profiling and acute-slice physiology
g.desc: The RNA embedding contains all observed CA1/prosubiculum nuclei from the P60 cohort. The nuclei micrograph and fluorescence sorting gate are literature examples. The Hi-C reference is from published cortical data. Dashed routes, the separate CA1 loop model and electrophysiology denote proposed measurements.

g.title: Mouse coronal section and enlarged dorsal hippocampus
g.desc: Atlas-based schematic. Dorsal is up and lateral is right. CA1 is highlighted in teal and the dentate granule cell layer is blue-grey. Adapted from the Allen Mouse Brain Atlas, adult coronal image 100960240. Anatomical reference © Allen Institute for Brain Science.

g.title: Chongtham et al., 2021, Fig. 3C: isolated unsorted sfGFP-positive mouse neocortical nuclei; source scale bar 25 µm (CC BY 4.0).
Butto et al., 2024, Fig. S2A: Arc–SUN1-GFP mouse brain nuclei sorting; original GFP-negative and GFP-positive single DAPI-positive nuclear gates (CC BY 4.0).
All CA1 and prosubiculum RNA coordinates, colored by five RNA-defined populations
Published cortical Hi-C map and a separate schematic of a putative CA1 enhancer–promoter contact.

Published bicuculline-treated, floxed mouse primary cortical neuron Hi-C matrix, chromosome 17. The upper triangle has been reoriented with genomic position along the base and separation increasing upward. Wahl et al., 2026, Figure 7A (CC BY 4.0).
Reciprocal paired recordings in an acute hippocampal slice
g.desc: Two glass pipettes each contact a soma. Stimulation of a CA1 pyramidal cell can evoke an excitatory current in its interneuron partner. Stimulation of the interneuron can evoke an inhibitory current in the pyramidal cell.
